title: Make a PS2 Buzz controller appear in PCSX2 on Windows
summary: Identify the Buzz receiver in Device Manager and select Windows USB Input Device only for that receiver when it is absent from PCSX2.
heroAlt: Wireless Buzz! quiz controllers and their receiver for PlayStation.
author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: make a ps2 buzz controller visible in windows
Make a PS2 Buzz controller appear in PCSX2 on Windows

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents a Windows case where Buzz controllers do not appear in the emulator. The receiver may show under Universal Serial Bus controllers as Standard USB HUB with a yellow warning icon. The documented workaround selects Windows USB Input Device for that receiver. This is a targeted driver change: never apply it to a neighboring hub or every controller.

Disconnect the Buzz receiver, close PCSX2, and note the existing Device Manager entry. Reconnect it and identify the entry that disappears and returns. If a vendor installer supplied the current driver, note its name and keep its uninstall or repair option available. Do not change an unidentified device.

items: 1. Connect the Buzz receiver and open Windows Device Manager.
2. Expand Universal Serial Bus controllers and locate the receiver; PCSX2 notes it may appear as Standard USB HUB with a yellow warning triangle.
3. Open Properties and confirm the entry changes when you unplug and reconnect the receiver.
4. Choose Update Driver > Browse my computer for drivers > Let me pick from a list of available drivers.
5. Select USB Input Device only for the identified Buzz receiver and confirm Windows’ prompt.
6. Close Device Manager, reconnect if requested, and restart PCSX2 if the device is not listed yet.

blocks.text: Pass when PCSX2 controller settings list the Buzz receiver as an available input source and the receiver remains visible in Device Manager after reconnecting. Map one button only after enumeration succeeds, then test it in a title menu. Device detection does not mean buttons have already been mapped.

items: No matching entry: reconnect and refresh Device Manager; do not change a neighboring hub.
PCSX2 still omits the receiver: fully close and reopen the emulator.
The receiver vanishes: use driver rollback or restore its recorded prior driver.
A vendor driver returns: check Installed apps for the matching Buzz package and use its own uninstall process.

blocks.text: Open the receiver Properties > Driver tab and select Roll Back Driver if available. Otherwise restore the recorded compatible driver through Update Driver. Reboot only if Windows requests it; confirm the receiver returns to its prior Device Manager state before reopening PCSX2.
